body.prompt: Turn the first image, a 3D render of Lisbon, Portugal, into a hyperrealistic real aerial photograph. The fourth image is a real photograph of the same view from a moment earlier in the same helicopter flight, re-projected into this camera (some parts may be soft, stretched or missing): the result must match it — the same roofs, colours, materials, trees, light, haze and photographic look wherever it shows them — and be equally sharp and real everywhere. Same camera, same framing, same field of view: a pixel-aligned photo, not a new composition. Do not zoom, crop, rotate or extend the view. The top of the picture is still city all the way to the top edge: no sky, no horizon and no sea there. Every box in the render is a simplified stand-in for a real old Lisbon building: redraw it as the real building it stands for, with its exact footprint, height and roof outline, real terracotta roof tiles, chimneys, roof terraces, real windows with shutters and balconies, weathered plaster in real colours, real trees, cars and streets. Streets, squares, the shoreline and every landmark stay exactly where they are. The second image is the exact depth map and the third the exact outlines of every building, roof and street: follow them.
